title: Associated graded ring of a combined polynomial ideal
statement: For a commutative ring R, ideal I⊆R and d≥0, set Q=IR[X_1,…,X_d]+(X_1,…,X_d) [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. There exists a ring isomorphism G:(gr_I R)[X_1,…,X_d]→gr_Q(R[X]) [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], taking the constant polynomial of every degree-n class [a], a∈I^n, to the degree-n class of the constant polynomial C(a). Each variable maps to a homogeneous degree-one class. The assertion includes I=0, I=R, the zero ring and d=0.

source.place: Tag 054L, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space; explicit polynomial-model calculation of lem-trf-smooth-rational-point-completion, Step 9 (not a verbatim assertion of that tag).

proof.text: Construct the canonical graded ring map induced by constants using the direct sum of the maps on ideal-power quotients. Define the polynomial evaluation map with these constants and degree-one classes of the variables. On a monomial with homogeneous coefficient [a] of degree k the result is [aX^E] in degree k+|E|, by the associated-graded multiplication formula.

On each degree-n quotient, extract the coefficient at E as its class in I^(n−|E|)/I^(n−|E|+1) when |E|≤n, and zero otherwise. The coefficient criterion makes these maps well defined on Q^n/Q^(n+1). Extend them additively across the direct sum. On the image of the evaluation map they return the polynomial coefficients, as checked first on homogeneous monomials and then by quotient and direct-sum induction. Therefore that ring map is injective.

Represent any homogeneous target class by p∈Q^n and write p as its finite sum of monomials. If |E|≤n, the corresponding monomial class is the image of X^E with coefficient [p_E] in degree n−|E|. If |E|>n, its monomial belongs to Q^(n+1) and gives zero. Thus every homogeneous class, and consequently every finite sum, is in the image. The bijective canonical ring map yields the claimed equivalence and compatibilities.

theorem combinedIdeal_associatedGraded
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (d : ℕ) :
    let Q := I.map (C (σ := Fin d)) ⊔ idealOfVars (Fin d) R
    ∃ G : MvPolynomial (Fin d) (Ideal.associatedGraded I) ≃+*
        Ideal.associatedGraded Q,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (a : R) (ha : a ∈ I ^ n) (hb : C a ∈ Q ^ n),
        G (C (DirectSum.of (Ideal.associatedGradedPiece I) n
          (Submodule.Quotient.mk (⟨a, ha⟩ : (I ^ n : Ideal R))))) =
            DirectSum.of (Ideal.associatedGradedPiece Q) n
              (Submodule.Quotient.mk (⟨C a, hb⟩ : (Q ^ n : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin d) R))))) ∧
      ∀ i : Fin d, ∃ z : Ideal.associatedGradedPiece Q 1,
        G (X i) = DirectSum.of (Ideal.associatedGradedPiece Q) 1 z
